newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia scraps alcohol import quota, orders licenses.
newsitem.headline: Russia scraps alcohol import quota, orders licenses.

text.p: Russia has scrapped an import quota on strong alcoholic drinks and ethanol that had been due to take effect on January 1, ordering instead that all imports be licensed, a State Customs Committee spokesman said on Friday.
"The import quotas were scrapped by a government resolution on December 30, just before they were due to come into effect," Vladimir Yemelyanov told Reuters.

"At the same time the government ordered the foreign trade ministry, the economy ministry and our committee to prepare to re-issue importers' licences within a month. Meanwhile old licences will be effective," he said.
In September Russia imposed import quotas for 1997 of 100 million litres of strong liquors and 10 million litres of ethanol in a bid to protect domestic producers.

An agriculture ministry official who declined to be named said the quota had been scrapped due to objections by the World Trade Organisation. Russia is seeking membership of the body this year and has recently liberalised its trade regime.
The International Monetary Fund also insisted late last year that Russia give up plans to introduce alcohol import quotas.
The IMF reviews Russia's economic performance and policies on a monthly basis to see if it is complying with the terms of a $10.2 billion three-year loan agreement struck in 1995.
Experts have estimated average annual imports of vodka and ethanol at 1.27 billion litres.
Interfax news agency quoted another source in the customs committee as saying all imports of alcohol had stopped as customs officials awaited new licences.
"Absolutely no way can we stop importing alcohol. Foreign vodka keeps coming into the country," Yemelyanov said.
